notable_absence.finding: Like both prior twins of this page (server/7.2 and cloud), the 8.0 Server page never states which role or privilege a user needs to create or edit a type mapping - prerequisites are only 'You have the Search Service enabled', 'You have created an index', and 'You have logged in'. This round supplies a partial resolution from a sibling page in the same batch: set-type-identifier.md (also 8.0, also a Search-index-editing task one click away from this one) DOES state a role - 'Your user account has the Search Admin role for the bucket where you want to edit an index' - but no page anywhere states whether that same role also gates creating/editing a type mapping specifically, so the gap on THIS page remains open rather than resolved.

cross_product_finding: Real divergence confirmed between this 8.0 Server page and its measured 0.30-similarity cloud/search/create-type-mapping.json twin, exactly as the round briefing predicted. The cloud/Capella page is built around XATTRs mappings and 'future field' mappings (both explicitly gated behind capella:advanced-mode), and its own next-steps point only to about-mappings.md and customize-index.md. The 8.0 Server page covers NEITHER of those two topics at all - Server 8.0 has split XATTRs mapping out into its own dedicated page, create-xattrs-mapping.md (also in this batch), which this page's Next Steps section does not even cross-link to (a real, if minor, missing seeAlso on the Server side: XATTRs mappings are 'child mappings for document metadata' by another name, yet create-type-mapping.md's Next Steps list every other customization task except that one). Instead, the Server page is structured as a hub for the static/dynamic mapping toggle and for the type-identifier/child-field/child-mapping task family, none of which the Capella twin surfaces on this page at all (Capella covers type identifiers via its own set-type-identifier equivalent, referenced only via customize-index.md's anchor). Confirms the briefing's framing: same task, same candidate_id, materially different scope and organization between the two surfaces.
